headline: Waller floats a 50bp Fed hike, dollar hits new 19-month high; pound slides on soft UK CPI
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.2% to a fresh 19-month high near 103.8 after Governor Waller argued for a half-point hike in December and the October minutes showed almost all officials expect further increases. Sterling, the Aussie and the ringgit lagged, while the yen held flat under Tokyo's 160 line and the won firmed on an Nvidia-led Kospi rebound.
drivers: The Fed debate moves to how big

Waller told CNBC the Fed may need to go 50bp on Dec 9 or clearly signal another hike, and the minutes showed a couple of officials open to more than 25bp. The 2-year yield held near 4.80% while a 4% drop in oil pulled the 10-year down to about 5.07%.
Soft UK services inflation hits sterling

UK CPI rose to 3.6% as expected, but core held at 2.8% and services cooled to 3.7%, so December BoE hike odds fell to about 80% from 92%. GBP/USD lost about 0.45% to near 1.3148, its weakest since late 2025.

Bank Indonesia surprised with a hike to 6.00%, the PBOC fixed at 6.7118, its strongest since 2022, and Taiwan's central bank held the Taiwan dollar below 33 as foreigners sold NT$76.6bn of shares; the won gained 5.2 to 1,333.0 as the Kospi rebounded 2%.
view: Bullish for the next 1–2 weeks: talk of a 50bp December hike widens the gap with the BoE, BoC and RBA, and I keep backing the dollar against the loonie, the pound and the Aussie, adding on dips rather than chasing. I still fade it against the yen near 160, where Tokyo is on guard. A DXY close below 102.5, or soft US data that pushes the 50bp talk out of the price, would turn me neutral.
ideas: Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100 as oil falls and the 2-year gap tops 148bp; for 1.4450, stop raised to 1.4250.
New short from 1.3150–1.3180 after soft UK services CPI broke the range; for 1.3000, stop 1.3240.
Hold the sale filled at 160.00–160.20 as Tokyo guards 160 and Ueda leans hawkish; for 157.50, stop cut to 160.50.
review: No target or stop was hit. EUR/USD is about 205 pips in favour, AUD/USD about 190, USD/CAD about 240, USD/JPY about 75, USD/CHF about 45 and EUR/JPY about 70, so I hold all and trail stops; the ringgit long is about 0.03 ahead and gets a 4.150 target. GBP/USD closed below its 1.3150 floor and turns short; the rupiah long and USD/INR short are roughly flat, and the other ranges held, with USD/TWD again pushed back from 33.

eurusd.note: Down about 0.2% to near 1.0974 after a new 19-month low around 1.0960; the short is about 205 pips in favour.
eurusd.why: The dollar did most of the moving. Waller's case for a 50bp December hike and minutes showing almost all officials expect more hikes kept the US 2-year near 4.80%, about 170bp over Bunds. The euro added its own drag: the French-German 10-year spread widened back to about 140bp on political worries, and an upward revision to core inflation (2.6%) gave it no help.
eurusd.outlook: I hold the short for 1.0900 and trail the stop to 1.1020, just above the broken 1.10 level: the Fed is set to outpace an ECB that is priced for only one more move. A close above 1.1020 would say the dollar's run has stalled.
eurusd.watch: Lagarde (Nov 19–20), euro zone consumer confidence (Nov 20), flash PMIs (late Nov), ECB (Dec 17).

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed outpaces ECB, French spread wider.

gbpusd.note: Down about 0.45% to near 1.3148, the weakest since late 2025, closing just below my 1.3150 range floor.
gbpusd.why: Sterling did the moving. October CPI rose to 3.6% as expected, but core held at 2.8% and services eased to 3.7%, just under forecasts, which MUFG read as limited pass-through risk. Traders cut the odds of a December BoE hike to about 80% from 92% earlier in the week, while the dollar was lifted by Waller's 50bp talk.
gbpusd.outlook: The close under 1.3150 turns me short toward 1.3000, near this year's 1.3137 low and beyond: BoE hike odds are slipping while the Fed's are rising. A close back above 1.3240 would say the break has failed.
gbpusd.watch: UK retail sales (Nov 20), BoE speakers, UK flash PMIs (late Nov), BoE (Dec 17).

view.call: Sell 1.3150–1.3180; soft services CPI trims BoE hike odds.

audusd.note: Down about 0.3% to near 0.6713, a new 10-month low; the sale is about 190 pips in favour.
audusd.why: The dollar did the moving, and strong local wages could not stop it. Q3 wage growth hit 1.1% q/q (1.0% expected), the fastest since late 2023, but swaps still see the RBA near its peak. Waller's 50bp talk, a 4% fall in oil and a slide in copper and gold weighed on commodity currencies late in the day.
audusd.outlook: I hold the sale for 0.6650, near January's lows, and trail the stop to 0.6755: the Fed is hiking while the RBA looks done. A strong jobs report that lifts the pair above 0.6755 would end the call.
audusd.watch: Australia jobs (Nov 19), RBA speakers, China loan prime rates (Nov 20), monthly CPI (Nov 25).

view.call: Sale from 0.6900–0.6920; Fed hiking, RBA near its peak.

usdjpy.note: Flat near 159.36 after an early rise to about 159.55; my sale from 160.00–160.20 is about 75 pips in favour.
usdjpy.why: Two forces cancelled out. Hawkish Fed minutes and Waller's 50bp talk kept the US 2-year firm near 4.80%, which normally lifts the pair. But BoJ Governor Ueda signalled further tightening, the 10-year Treasury yield fell about 3.5bp to 5.07% as oil dropped, and Tokyo's warnings near 160 kept buyers cautious, so the yen held its ground.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the sale for 157.50 and cut the stop to 160.50, above Friday's 160.19 high: Tokyo has capped the pair below 160 with words all month and a BoJ hike is in play. A close above 160.50 would show Tokyo is standing aside.
usdjpy.watch: Japan CPI (Nov 20), Tokyo comments near 160, BoJ speakers, Japan's monthly intervention data (Nov 30).

view.call: Sale filled 160.00–160.20; Tokyo guards 160, BoJ leans hawkish.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.3% to near 0.8434, another 18-month high; my long is about 45 pips in favour.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving against a zero-yielding franc. With Waller pushing for a bigger December hike and the minutes showing broad support for more, the rate gap with the SNB's 0% keeps widening, and the franc continues to fund carry trades. Even with the Dow down more than 1% and gold falling, the franc drew no haven demand.
usdchf.outlook: I hold the long for 0.8500 and raise the stop to 0.8390: the rate gap is widening and the franc is not acting as a haven. A close back below 0.8390 would say the breakout has failed.
usdchf.watch: Fed speakers, SNB comments, Swiss CPI (early Dec), Fed (Dec 8–9).

view.call: Long 0.8380–0.8400; rate gap, franc used to fund carry.

usdcad.note: Up about 0.3% to near 1.4330 after a new 19-month high of 1.4340; the buy is about 240 pips in favour.
usdcad.why: Both sides helped. Waller's hawkish comments lifted the dollar, and US crude fell about 4% to near $82.50 after inventory data pointed to a supply surplus, hurting the oil-linked loonie. The US 2-year yield now sits about 148bp above Canada's, roughly 21bp wider than at the start of November, with the Bank of Canada on hold.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the buy for 1.4450 and raise the stop to 1.4250: the policy gap is the widest of this cycle and oil is sliding. A sharp oil rebound or a dovish Fed turn would be the main threats.
usdcad.watch: Canada retail sales (Nov 20), oil and Hormuz headlines, BoC speakers, Canada Q3 GDP (late Nov).

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; BoC on hold, Fed hiking, oil down.

usdcnh.note: Little changed near 6.668 offshore despite the strongest PBOC fixing since July 2022.
usdcnh.why: The PBOC and the dollar pulled in opposite directions. The midpoint was raised to 6.7118, the strongest since 2022, but it was still about 460 pips weaker than the 6.6654 estimate, so Beijing is allowing only gradual gains as Xi meets Trump at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. The broad dollar rally on Waller's comments kept the offshore yuan from extending.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: fixings lean against a faster rally while exporters sell dollars on bounces. A close below 6.64 after the summit would show Beijing is letting the yuan run.
usdcnh.watch: APEC Xi-Trump meeting (Nov 19), loan prime rates (Nov 20), daily fixings vs estimates.

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, exporters sell USD.

usdhkd.note: Steady near 7.8451, about 50 pips from the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved it. The wide gap between US rates and HIBOR, now growing as the Fed debates a bigger hike, keeps the carry trade into US dollars attractive and holds the Hong Kong dollar near the weak end of its band. The HKMA's 7.85 commitment caps the pair.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: carry keeps it near 7.85, and only a HIBOR jump or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Up slightly to near 1.2893, inside my 1.2780–1.2920 range and just under 1.29.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving, gently. Waller's 50bp talk lifted the pair toward 1.29, but the Singapore dollar again outperformed most regional peers, gaining against the ringgit and the Taiwan dollar, because the MAS policy band keeps it well supported against its trade-weighted basket.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2780–1.2920 range: the MAS band anchors the Singapore dollar while a hiking Fed keeps the pair firm. A close above 1.2920 would open 1.3000.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore final Q3 GDP and CPI (late Nov), Fed speakers, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won rose 5.2 to 1,333.0 in Seoul after touching 1,328.4 as the Kospi rebounded 2% to 5,067.
usdkrw.why: Risk appetite did the moving. Nvidia's beat and $130bn guidance lifted Samsung and SK hynix and pulled the Kospi back above 5,000, and exporters sold dollars at the open. Gains faded later as the dollar strengthened globally and importers bought, and foreigners were still net sellers of about 334bn won of shares.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: exporter selling caps the pair, while continued foreign stock selling and a hawkish Fed limit won gains. A Seoul close below 1,325 would open 1,315; above 1,365 would revive the long.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, Fed speakers, oil, Korea November exports (Dec 1).

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 9.7 cents to 32.947, its weakest close since April 2025, after touching 33.023.
usdtwd.why: Foreign outflows did the moving. Foreigners sold NT$76.6bn of Taiwan shares on index futures settlement day, about NT$180bn over three sessions, and their dollar buying pushed the pair through 33 for a second day. Exporters sold near 33 and local reports said the central bank stepped in during the final half hour to keep the close below 33.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials are clearly defending 33 and exporters sell there, but outflows cap the Taiwan dollar. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed; below 32.60 would open 32.40.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, central bank action near 33, Taiwan export orders (Nov 20), central bank meeting (mid-Dec).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit fell to 4.1130/1180 at the 6pm KL close from 4.0915/0960; my long is about 0.03 in favour.
usdmyr.why: The dollar did the moving. Bank Muamalat's chief economist pointed to the hawkish US rate outlook as traders weighed a bigger Fed hike on Dec 9, and the ringgit also lost ground to the Singapore dollar, yen, euro and pound. Lower oil and palm oil prices removed some support for Malaysia's export earnings.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the long, lift the target to 4.150 and raise the stop to 4.090: Fed hikes outweigh Bank Negara's steady rate. A close back below 4.090 would say the break has failed.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia October CPI (late Nov), oil and palm oil, regional chip stocks, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 4.080–4.090; Fed hike bets outweigh a steady BNM.

usdphp.note: Peso slipped 4 centavos to 63.71 at the BAP close in a tight 63.53–63.75 range.
usdphp.why: Two forces offset each other. RCBC's Ricafort said fresh US-Iran attacks weighed on the peso, while lower global oil prices, the key driver of the import bill, limited the damage. Traders said there was no strong catalyst, and turnover fell to $1.27bn from $1.49bn.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.30–64.20 range with the record low as the cap: falling oil, holiday remittances and possible BSP hikes help, but the Fed weighs. A close above 64.20 would mark a new record and open 64.80.
usdphp.watch: Oil and Middle East headlines, BSP comments, Fed speakers, BSP decision (Dec 17).

view.call: 63.30–64.20; oil, remittances and BSP vs Fed.

usdidr.note: Rupiah firmed about 0.1% to 18,220 after a surprise BI hike to 6.00%; JISDOR 18,252. Long roughly flat.
usdidr.why: Bank Indonesia did the moving, but only a little. It raised rates 25bp to 6.00%, a move only 10 of 27 economists expected, taking hikes since May to 125bp, after the rupiah hit a record 18,285 on Tuesday. The rupiah turned from a 0.13% loss to a small gain, while the Jakarta index fell 1.1% as political turmoil and Fed bets kept pressure on.
usdidr.outlook: I hold the long for 18,500 with the stop at 18,150: a 0.1% gain on a surprise hike shows the market is not convinced, and politics and outflows persist. A close below 18,150 would show BI has turned the tide.
usdidr.watch: BI follow-up comments and intervention, MSCI changes (effective Nov 30), politics, Fed speakers.

view.call: Long 18,200–18,250; hike failed to lift rupiah, outflows persist.

usdinr.note: Rupee rose 7 paise to about 93.44, another seven-month high, after trading 93.25–93.57.
usdinr.why: Lower oil did the moving, and the strong dollar limited it. Brent's drop toward $89 cuts importers' dollar needs and recent foreign portfolio inflows kept supporting the rupee, which touched 93.25 intraday. Gains were pared as Indian stocks fell and the dollar index rose about 0.3% on hawkish Fed talk.
usdinr.outlook: I hold the short for 92.90 and trim the stop to 93.75: inflows and cheaper oil are doing the work. RBI dollar buying to rebuild reserves is the main risk; a close above 93.75 would end the call.
usdinr.watch: Foreign equity flows, oil, India flash PMIs (late Nov), RBI decision (Dec 4).

view.call: Sell 93.50–93.60; FPI inflows and cheaper oil.

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.25% to near 174.88; my sale is about 70 pips in favour.
eurjpy.why: The euro did the moving. It slipped against the dollar as the French-German spread widened again, while the yen held flat on Ueda's hawkish tone and Tokyo's watch over 160. With USD/JPY unchanged, the cross simply tracked EUR/USD lower.
eurjpy.outlook: I hold the sale, extend the target to 173.50 and trail the stop to 175.80: the euro is losing ground and the yen is protected near 160. A close back above 175.80 would say the old range has resumed.
eurjpy.watch: Lagarde (Nov 19–20), Japan CPI (Nov 20), Tokyo comments, euro zone PMIs (late Nov).

view.call: Sell 175.4–175.8; weak euro, yen guarded near 160.

cnhjpy.note: Little changed near 23.90, mid-way in my 23.6–24.2 range.
cnhjpy.why: Neither side moved. The yuan held near a two-week high on the strongest PBOC fixing since 2022 as the APEC summit began, and USD/JPY was flat below 160, so the cross barely changed. Both currencies are anchored by officials: Beijing slows the yuan, Tokyo caps the yen's losses.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.6–24.2 range: the cross follows USD/JPY, which Tokyo is likely to cap near 160. A close above 24.2 would show intervention is not coming.
cnhjpy.watch: APEC Xi-Trump meeting (Nov 19), PBOC fixings, Japan CPI (Nov 20).

view.call: 23.6–24.2; yen near Tokyo's line, yuan held.

eurcnh.note: Down about 0.2% to near 7.317, in the lower half of my 7.28–7.40 range.
eurcnh.why: The euro did the moving. It fell against the dollar on Fed hike talk and wider French spreads, while the offshore yuan held steady after the PBOC set its strongest fixing since 2022 as China hosts APEC. The cross drifted lower with EUR/USD.
eurcnh.outlook: I keep a 7.28–7.40 range with a downward tilt: euro weakness should continue while the PBOC slows yuan gains. A close below 7.28 would open 7.22.
eurcnh.watch: APEC summit (Nov 19), PBOC fixings, Lagarde (Nov 19–20), euro zone PMIs (late Nov).

view.call: 7.28–7.40; weak euro vs PBOC brake on yuan.

watch: Next: Australia jobs, Lagarde and the APEC Xi-Trump meeting (Nov 19), Japan CPI, China's loan prime rates and UK and Canada retail sales (Nov 20), flash PMIs and US PCE (late Nov), then the RBI (Dec 4), Fed (Dec 8–9) and ECB, BoE and BSP (Dec 17), plus Tokyo's 160 line and Taiwan's defence of 33.
